items.title: Jonathan Scales interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 23, 2025
items.q: I’ve been able to speak with Howard Levy and Bela Fleck and the three of you are playing an instrument that you’ve stretched the boundaries of

ctx.x: Yeah I mean so January makes 19 years of me doing this with my band. And yeah, it’s always a – it’s like it’s always a constant flow but you know it’s a whole process. So like you don’t start at the beginning thinking about all of this stuff. You just start. And then as things go along you have to morph and you have to figure things out. You know? So like I don’t even know where to begin – that’s a whole deep dive in itself, of like career sustainability. You know? But I will say that like for me as a band leader…

I do. And it’s interesting because I’ve been able to speak with Howard Levy and Bela Fleck and the three of you are playing an instrument that you’ve stretched the boundaries of, and not necessarily the everyday oh saxophone, piano, trumpet. Do you believe that that distinction is a plus in some ways and a minus in others as far as marketing?

Oh yes. Yes. It’s a gift and a curse. Because the gift is, “Oh wow, like how is this person doing this on this instrument that I’ve never seen before. I’m instantly drawn into this. Like this looks cool, what could this possibly be?” So you do get that side of it, right? But © Fillius Jazz Archive -16-
